body_markdown:
In the[last post in our Tradeweb Ai-Price blog series](https://www.tradeweb.com/newsroom/media-center/insights/blog/tradeweb-ai-price-evolving-credit-pricing-for-todays-market/) , we briefly went through the methodology of our enhanced pricing algorithm and explored its accuracy across the liquidity spectrum. In this piece, we highlight a few key inputs that help drive model performance and reflect Tradeweb’s view of how[credit markets](https://www.tradeweb.com/our-markets/institutional/credit/) actually trade. With our global client footprint and diverse range of clients, we can supplement public market data with our proprietary datasets and market signals.


#### Cleaning up TRACE & conflation


TRACE is a major input to our pricing algorithm and is the source for many of the features both at the bond level and across issuers, sectors and ratings. However, using the raw TRACE feed can be problematic due to the many nuances of how different trading protocols print on TRACE. As the trading of U.S. corporate bonds across investment-grade and high-yield becomes increasingly electronic, especially with the rise of multi-legged trades, details of an exact economic transaction on the TRACE tape can become harder to decipher.


As an established operator of many of these trading protocols, we have a differentiated view of how activity across these workflows is reflected in TRACE. Since we know how our different trading protocols print on TRACE, we can more accurately interpret the economic details of each of those transactions than the raw TRACE feed alone allows. This is a critical data cleaning exercise for our pricing algorithm as we can ‘conflate’ trades together into a single economic transaction, allowing us to discard noise and focus on the most informative elements of the trade to inform our price.


#### Delayed spots


Moreover, in IG credit where bonds mostly trade in spread to a Treasury benchmark, many clients choose to delay the point at which they ‘spot’ their trades – i.e. snapshot the Treasury to which the price of the bond they are trading is calculated against. With more than a decade of experience supporting spotting workflows in credit markets, Tradeweb has developed a deep understanding of how these trades are executed and reported. Through our multi-client net spotting protocols, clients and dealers can net their spots at certain times throughout the day.


This means that, for trades executed on Tradeweb we know the ‘true’ trade times associated with these transactions, including the actual time and spread level at which the corporate bond was agreed earlier in the day (as well as the full stack of responses). We are therefore able to incorporate these trades into our pricing algorithm at the time the trade was agreed rather than having to wait until later in the day, by which time the level may be stale.


#### Leveraging European credit and retail data


Tradeweb’s global footprint provides additional proprietary signals from activity on our European credit and retail platforms. The model uses aggregated changes across these data streams as additional inputs to help infer market direction. These signals can supplement sparse TRACE observations and help the model estimate changes in spread, particularly for less liquid corporate bonds. They can also provide a broader view of market moves that may be difficult to discern from TRACE alone.


#### Asset manager case study


Throughout our research process, we collaborated with clients to work towards building a product which met their expectations as a state-of-the-art composite price. One large asset manager took our Ai-Price sample data and ran tests compared to competitor pricing algorithms. They looked at $1 million+ TRACE prints across dealer buys/sells and dealer-to-dealer trades for a subset of IG securities from March-April 2026 to compare against our bids, offers and mids. Below, they plotted the absolute errors compared to the next TRACE print, which showed lower errors for Ai-Price than for the competitor pricing algorithms tested across these trade types in the sample set and particularly in the lower end of the liquidity spectrum. This result reflects the advanced machine-learning techniques at the core of our methodology as well as the proprietary datasets that power our model inputs.


####


####
Conclusion


Ai-Price combines enhanced TRACE data with proprietary Tradeweb signals, including institutional RFQ activity, retail activity and European credit activity, alongside broader macro signals from credit default swap indices and ETF markets. Together, we believe these inputs help provide a more complete view of U.S. corporate bond pricing and market conditions.


As with all Tradeweb products, collaboration with clients was essential in the development process, with a large asset manager providing feedback that they believe we are the best in class for their IG universe compared to other products they evaluated. We look forward to continuing to collaborate with our clients and incorporating their feedback in the future.


This enhanced model is currently available for IG and HY corporate bonds, and we’re actively working towards expanding coverage across additional fixed income products, including emerging market bonds. This continued development is designed to broaden the applications of Ai-Price across pricing, automation and portfolio analytics.


Stay tuned for our next piece, where we will explore the applications of Ai-Price, starting with our pre-trade analytics.
